title: THE TENTH THAT IS THE LORD'S

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'A tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or
fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD. Whoever
would redeem any of their tithe must add a fifth of the value to it'"
- Lev 27:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A tenth of everything the land produced belonged to the Lord. Notice the
wording carefully: the tithe already belongs to the Lord; it is holy to
the Lord. It was not a gift the people generously decided to give. It was
God's portion, set apart as already His.

That distinction matters. In Israel, the tithe was a regular, tangible
way of acknowledging that God was the true source of every harvest. Each
tenth returned to Him said, "This all came from You."

Dear friend, believers today hold different convictions about tithing —
whether the tenth is a binding rule under the new covenant or a helpful
principle that points to something greater. Sincere Christians land in
different places, and we need not divide over it. But the heart behind it
speaks to all of us.

The New Testament lifts the focus from a percentage to the whole
disposition of the heart. Paul says each of you should give what you have
decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for
God loves a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7). Jesus affirmed careful giving but
warned against tithing herbs while neglecting justice and mercy (Matt
23:23).

Whatever pattern of giving you follow, let it flow from a heart that
genuinely acknowledges God as the source of everything you have. Give
regularly, give cheerfully, and give as worship — not as a bill to be
paid.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does my giving acknowledge God as the source of all I have?
2. Do I give cheerfully, or reluctantly and out of obligation?
3. Is my giving regular and intentional, or an afterthought?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are the source of everything I have. Make me a cheerful,
regular giver whose giving is real worship, flowing from a grateful heart.
Amen.
